sentences.text: Irritator was estimated to be between 6 and 8 meters long and weigh around 1 ton, making it one of the smallest known spinosaurids.
It possessed a long, shallow, and slender snout lined with straight, unserrated conical teeth.
A thin sagittal crest ran along the top of its head, likely anchoring powerful neck muscles.
Its nostrils were positioned far back on the snout, and a rigid secondary palate likely strengthened its jaw during feeding.
The holotype specimen of Irritator challengeri is a subadult and represents the most completely preserved spinosaurid skull ever found.
The genus Irritator was described by Martill et al. in 1996.
The holotype skull was acquired by fossil dealers and sold to the State Museum of Natural History Stuttgart.
The genus name Irritator refers to the irritation paleontologists felt because the skull was heavily damaged and altered by collectors.
The species name challengeri honors the fictional character Professor Challenger from Arthur Conan Doyle's novels.
Researchers suggest Irritator had a generalist diet similar to modern crocodilians, likely preying mainly on fish and other small animals.
Fossil evidence indicates an individual Irritator ate a pterosaur, either by hunting or scavenging.
Irritator may have had semiaquatic habits and lived in a tropical coastal lagoon environment surrounded by dry regions.
Irritator was identified as a spinosaurid theropod in 1996.
The holotype skull was redescribed in 2002, confirming its classification as a spinosaurid.
Both Irritator and Angaturama belong to the Spinosaurinae subfamily.
Irritator lived during the middle Cretaceous, approximately 110 million years ago in the Albian stage, in what is now South America.
Irritator was found in the Santana Formation in Brazil.
The specimen most probably originates from the Romualdo Formation, though the exact site is uncertain due to trafficking.
Local dealers suggested the fossil came from near the village of Buxexé at a height of approximately 650 meters.
Angaturama limai was described in February 1996 by Alexander W. A. Kellner and Diogenes de Almeida Campos.
Some paleontologists consider Angaturama limai a potential junior synonym of Irritator.
Multiple authors from 2002 to 2015 supported the conclusion that Angaturama is a synonym of Irritator.
Kellner and Campos, and later Machado and Kellner, argued that the fossils belong to two different genera because the Angaturama holotype is more laterally flattened.
If the two genera are the same, Irritator is the valid name because it was published almost a month before Angaturama.
